# Where `sandbox-capture.json` came from

Captured **2026-07-26** from Oura's public sandbox:

```
https://api.ouraring.com/v2/sandbox/usercollection/{scope}
  ?start_date=2024-01-01&end_date=2024-01-07
```

13 scopes, 73 records. Re-capture with `pnpm --filter @open-twin/provider-oura capture:sandbox`.

## Why this instead of hand-written fixtures

Every mapper test previously ran on literals someone typed while writing the mapper.
That is the failure this whole remediation is about, one level down: a fixture
written from the same understanding as the code cannot contradict the code. It
agrees with the author's mental model whether or not the model is right.

This capture disagrees with us where we were wrong. The first sleep record reads:

```
total_sleep_duration  2370      (seconds — 39.5 minutes)
time_in_bed           3000      (seconds — 50 minutes)
latency               50
efficiency            70
```

Durations in seconds under LOINC codes whose example unit is minutes is precisely
defect O3, and the shape of the real payload is what makes it obvious.

## What it is, and is not

**Synthetic.** Oura describes the sandbox as fake user data, generated by Oura and
not derived from real users, served without an account. It is not anybody's health
record and it is safe to commit.

**Not a faithful oracle for the published spec.** The sandbox and the OpenAPI
document disagree in at least one place: `heartrate` rows here carry
`producer_timestamp`, which the spec does not declare, and omit `timestamp_unix`,
which the spec marks required. Treat spec conformance and sandbox conformance as
two separate signals; a test asserting one does not establish the other.

**`personal_info` is absent.** That path returns 404 in the sandbox — the spec
declares no sandbox route for it. This matters beyond the fixture: the connector's
`SUPPORTED_SCOPES` includes `personal_info` and `getOuraDataSandbox` passes
`sandbox: true` for every requested type, so any sandbox call including it fails.

**No credentials.** The sandbox accepts any non-empty bearer token, so the capture
script and the contract test run on a fork PR with no secrets.

## Privacy

The capture is deterministic: keys are sorted, so two consecutive runs are
byte-identical and a future diff shows a vendor change rather than a reshuffle.

Scanned for email, telephone, national-identifier and IBAN patterns at capture
time; zero matches, asserted by a test rather than by this sentence. An earlier
scan reported 266 "phone numbers" — all of them ISO dates matched by a careless
regex. Recorded because a privacy check nobody has falsified is not evidence.
